reports.title: UK Electricity Mix Weekly Report: Monday 7 September
reports.intro: A measured weekly report for EnergyMix.info using the available 7-day historical generation feed for Tuesday 1 September to Sunday 6 September.
reports.summary: The week from Tuesday 1 September to Sunday 6 September averaged about 26.2 GW of measured generation, with renewables averaging 50.5% of measured output. The strongest renewable day in the available data was Sunday 6 September, when wind, solar and hydro together averaged 56.0% of measured generation. Gas was highest on Wednesday 2 September and lowest on Thursday 3 September.
reports.takeaway: For flexible electricity use, the cleanest opportunities are likely to appear when wind is strong, gas is low and demand is not at a peak. This is the foundation for future EV-charging guidance, clean-electricity alerts and weekly newsletter summaries.
drivers: Renewables were strongest on Sunday 6 September, when wind, solar and hydro averaged 56.0% of measured generation.
Wind was the largest swing factor in the available feed, peaking at about 13.2 GW average output on Friday 4 September.
Solar was strongest on Saturday 5 September, averaging about 4.0 GW across settlement periods after embedded-solar backfill where needed.
Gas averaged about 4.8 GW across the period, rising highest on Wednesday 2 September and falling lowest on Thursday 3 September.
Measured generation was highest on Friday 4 September, at roughly 27.9 GW average output.

cleanestPeriods.title: Best low-carbon proxy: Sunday 6 September
cleanestPeriods.body: Historical carbon-intensity aggregates are not yet part of this weekly report feed, so EnergyMix.info uses renewable share and gas output as cautious proxies. Sunday 6 September had the strongest renewable share at 56.0%.

cleanestPeriods.title: Lowest gas proxy: Thursday 3 September
cleanestPeriods.body: Gas generation averaged about 3.5 GW on Thursday 3 September. Lower gas periods are often cleaner, but the report does not yet claim this was the lowest-carbon period without historical carbon-intensity validation.

higherCarbonPeriods.title: Highest gas proxy: Wednesday 2 September
higherCarbonPeriods.body: Gas averaged about 9.0 GW on Wednesday 2 September. Gas-heavy periods are usually higher-carbon, but this is labelled as a proxy until historical carbon-intensity highs/lows are added to the report feed.

socialPosts.title: Monday weekly grid brief
socialPosts.body:
Last week in Britain’s electricity mix:

• Highest renewable share in the available feed: 56.0% on Sunday 6 September
• Highest average wind output: ~13.2 GW on Friday 4 September
• Highest average solar output: ~4.0 GW on Saturday 5 September
• Highest average gas output: ~9.0 GW on Wednesday 2 September

The shift was clear: gas-heavy weekdays gave way to a cleaner, wind-led weekend.

Full report: https://energymix.info/reports/weekly/2026-09-07/

socialPosts.title: Wednesday explainer
socialPosts.body:
What does “UK electricity mix” actually mean?

For live grid dashboards, it usually means Great Britain’s electricity system: England, Scotland and Wales. Northern Ireland is part of the UK, but operates in a separate electricity market.

Explainer: https://energymix.info/uk-electricity-mix

socialPosts.title: Friday practical clean-electricity post
socialPosts.body:
The cleanest time to use electricity is not a fixed hour.

It changes with wind, solar, demand, imports and gas generation. Windy overnight periods and sunny middays can be much cleaner than still early-evening peaks.

Guide: https://energymix.info/cleanest-time-to-use-electricity
